card.title: Ki-61-I-TEI
card.text: Destruction: Deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ, give yours +2 defense.
card.flavorText: The Ki-61-I-TEI was a late-war variant of the Kawasaki Ki-61 Hien fighter, distinguished primarily by its upgraded armament and design adjustments aimed at improving firepower and maintainability. Introduced in 1944, the TEI model replaced the two 12.7 mm Ho-103 machine guns in the wings with 20 mm Ho-5 cannons, giving it significantly more destructive capability. The Ho-5, a Japanese design derived from the American Browning M2, was relatively light and compact but offered a high rate of fire and a heavier shell. This made the TEI version more effective against increasingly durable Allied aircraft. The TEI retained the Ki-61’s inline, liquid-cooled Ha-40 engine, a licensed version of the German DB 601. While the engine was advanced for a Japanese fighter, it remained maintenance-heavy and vulnerable in combat conditions. The aircraft’s structure, which included self-sealing fuel tanks and some pilot armor, reflected a growing Japanese concern for survivability by 1944. Despite improvements, production and deployment of the TEI variant were limited due to engine shortages and Allied bombing of Japanese industrial centers. It saw service defending the Japanese home islands and in units deployed to Okinawa and the Philippines. Roughly 1,380 Ki-61-I-TEI aircraft were produced before production ended.
